dosing.mania: start 750 mg/day (or 20-30 mg/kg/day), titrate rapidly to response; can be loaded (20 mg/kg/day oral loading for acute mania in some protocols)

teratogenicity.note: Malformations 10-11% overall, neural tube defects 1-2%, plus increased risk of neurodevelopmental impairment (lower IQ) and autism; NICE: do not start in women of childbearing potential unless pregnancy prevention programme in place and other options inadequate

hyperammonemia.note: Can occur with normal LFTs; causes lethargy, confusion, vomiting, increased seizure frequency; check ammonia if encephalopathic; risk increased with UCD and carnitine deficiency

thrombocytopenia.note: Dose-related; platelet count should be monitored especially at doses >45 mg/kg/day; bruising/bleeding warrants count

PCOS.note: Increased risk of menstrual irregularities, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries in women with epilepsy on valproate (evidence strongest in epilepsy)

monitoring.schedule: LFTs and FBC at 6 months, then every 12 months; weight at 3, 6, 12 months then annually; plasma level if poor response or toxicity suspected
monitoring.pregnancy_prevention_programme: annual specialist review; pregnancy test before starting and during; contraception counseling; patient card/acknowledgement form (MHRA/EMA measures)
